paragraphs: Swamiji asked his listeners to think hard about what they really mean by heaven. If heaven is just a place of endless sense pleasure, he said, it would be the worst curse imaginable for the soul, because we would stop growing. Is that all life comes to? A bit of crying, a bit of dancing, and then death? When we long only for the pleasures of this world, it shows we have not yet discovered what true joy is. Philosophy does not ask us to give up joy; it asks us to find out what joy really is.

To make the point, he described the heaven of the old Norse people. There, everyone sits before the god Odin. They go out on a wild boar hunt, then go to war and hack each other to pieces. Somehow, after a few hours of fighting, all their wounds heal. They head into a great hall, where the boar has been roasted, and feast and celebrate. The next day the boar comes back to life, ready to be hunted all over again.

Swamiji's verdict was blunt. Our own popular ideas of heaven are not much better, just a little more polished. Deep down we also want to keep hunting our wild boars and reach a place where the enjoyment never stops, just like the Norse warrior with his boar that is chased, eaten and back again every morning.
learn: Many of our dreams of the perfect life are really just today's pleasures on repeat: more food, more fun, more stuff. Ask yourself what would truly satisfy you, not just entertain you. That question is where real happiness begins.
